title: Caluma builds the form and the workflow but leaves the workflow state itself mutable
content:
Caluma is a form-and-workflow toolkit: it defines what a case looks like and the states it moves through. The gap the research identifies is narrow and specific — the workflow state itself is mutable. The current status is stored and updated in place, so what the workflow decided at each step is not preserved as a separate record that cannot be rewritten.

The commercial shape here is unusual within the corpus. Adfinis wrote Caluma, so this is not a pitch aimed at a tool the firm happens to use; it is co-development on their own product. The gap is theirs to close, closing it improves something they sell, and that changes both who has to be convinced and what the deliverable looks like.

It also raises the bar on precision. When the counterpart authored the tool, a description of its limits has to be exactly right or the credibility of the entire argument goes with it. The claim to make is the one the research supports — the workflow state is mutable — without inflating it into a verdict on the rest of Caluma.
